- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or adjust downward 1–2 days later.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 10-day moving average, consider mean reversion bias and reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day starting from day 10.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (days 20–30) prices when sentiment is positive; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to end of forecast.
